methodology: Articles sourced from Virginia-specific RSS feeds and Google News RSS, filtered for AI/technology/workforce relevance, then assessed by Claude against the scenario framework. Each article is tagged with the region it most affects and the scenario it signals toward.

signals.title: AI Ready Roanoke evaluates use for new technology in Roanoke Valley - Roanoke Times
signals.signal_reading: Community-driven AI fluency initiative in Roanoke Valley signals grassroots capability building outside major metros, representing distributed peer learning that could bridge the metro-rural divide if sustained beyond initial evaluation phase.

signals.title: Amazon bows to local backlash over AI data centers, scraps plans to build four new facilities in Northern Virginia — site to be repurposed for mixed-use and residential development. - Tom's Hardware
signals.signal_reading: Amazon's cancellation of four NoVA data centers reflects infrastructure backlash without evidence of local AI capability development—communities rejecting concentration while lacking distributed alternatives, potentially leaving the region with neither depth nor broad adoption.

signals.title: Amazon partnership advances AI and cybersecurity education at the Cyber Range - Virginia Tech News
signals.signal_reading: Amazon-Virginia Tech Cyber Range partnership deepens institutional AI/cybersecurity expertise but concentrates advanced learning in established tech education hubs, reinforcing capability concentration unless workforce pipelines actively distribute graduates to underserved regions.

signals.title: Virginia Orders AI Cybersecurity Plan as States Fill Federal Safety Gaps - PYMNTS.com
signals.signal_reading: Statewide AI cybersecurity planning directive creates potential for distributed platform-based AI adoption across state agencies, but top-down mandate risks shallow implementation without deep technical capacity building in regional government offices.

signals.title: Virginia Tech tests thermal cameras and AI to warn drivers of animals near roads - WDBJ7
signals.signal_reading: Virginia Tech's applied AI research for wildlife collision prevention demonstrates deep technical capability emanating from academic centers, but practical deployment requires transfer mechanisms to distribute AI problem-solving capacity to transportation departments statewide.
